about: FCI-JCI's own published measurements, one file per lane; the release summary's FCI-JCI entries are built from it
build: Andrey pre-release build of 6 November 2026 (version string 0.14.0); refitted on the 0.15.0 release branch of the same day, Andrey's two gated arms returned the same PAG on all 720 fits
comparator: pcalg 2.7-12 fci with jci = "1" and jci = "123", the implementation of FCI-JCI by the method's authors
verdict_rule: per cell, assumption set (jci = "1" with confounded_index=True, jci = "123" with confounded_index=False), and level: D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(pcalg) per dataset, on the datasets both finished; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise; a row with fewer than 10 paired datasets is reported, not judged; better or worse counts only if a rerun on seeds 100-119 agrees. 10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0). An in-claim row also fails when Andrey timed out on a dataset pcalg finished. Floor: the floor applies only where pcalg's interval of SHD minus the empty graph's lies wholly below 0, and there Andrey's must lie wholly below 0 too
fit_protocol: each fit in a fresh interpreter on one core with one BLAS thread, after one untimed warm-up fit (pcalg's warm-up only at 4 and 10 variables, where it cannot double a fit that may reach the cap); a cap of 1,800 s per fit with imports and warm-up, past which a fit is a timeout, never an empty graph; Andrey's time runs from the array in memory to the returned graph, pcalg's is the transfer into R, cor(X), and the call; ratio is the median over the paired datasets of pcalg's time over Andrey's
error_metric: shd: the endpoint SHD over the data variables and the environment against FCI-JCI's PAG at the true distribution under the same assumptions: variable pairs whose two endpoint marks differ, so a missing or extra edge costs both. andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, and the _mean fields their means
seeds_note: seeds is the number of datasets per setting: 20 (seeds 0-19) in every cell but P20 and P50, which ran 10 (seeds 0-9). pcalg was not run on P50, X100, X100m: on the dry run's two datasets of each (seeds 0 and 1), every pcalg fit, at both assumption sets and every level, timed out at the 1,800 s cap, and the campaign runs pcalg on such a cell only where it finished a dry-run fit; Andrey's rows there are reported against the empty graph. No in-claim row came out better or worse, so no rerun ran

cells.S4: S4: the simulation of Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen 2020 (Sec. 5.2, linear Gaussian, acyclic, with hidden confounders), small, mechanism change: 4 system variables, eps = eta = 0.5, 1 context variable, mechanism changes, 500 rows per regime (1,000 rows); in claim
cells.S4p: S4p: the simulation of Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen 2020 (Sec. 5.2, linear Gaussian, acyclic, with hidden confounders), small, perfect intervention: 4 system variables, eps = eta = 0.5, 1 context variable, perfect interventions, 500 rows per regime (1,000 rows); in claim
cells.L10: L10: the simulation of Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen 2020 (Sec. 5.2, linear Gaussian, acyclic, with hidden confounders), larger: 10 system variables, eps = eta = 0.25, 1 context variable, mechanism changes, 500 rows per regime (1,000 rows); in claim
cells.X100: X100: the simulation of Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen 2020 (Sec. 5.2, linear Gaussian, acyclic, with hidden confounders), large: 100 system variables, eps = eta = 0.02, 1 context variable, mechanism changes, 100 rows per regime (200 rows); in claim, where pcalg finishes
cells.S4m: S4m: the simulation of Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen 2020 (Sec. 5.2, linear Gaussian, acyclic, with hidden confounders), small, the paper's 2 context variables merged into one environment: 4 system variables, eps = eta = 0.5, 2 context variables, mechanism changes, 500 rows per regime (1,500 rows); out of claim
cells.L10m: L10m: the simulation of Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen 2020 (Sec. 5.2, linear Gaussian, acyclic, with hidden confounders), larger, the paper's 10 context variables merged into one environment: 10 system variables, eps = eta = 0.25, 10 context variables, mechanism changes, 500 rows per regime (5,500 rows); out of claim
cells.X100m: X100m: the simulation of Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen 2020 (Sec. 5.2, linear Gaussian, acyclic, with hidden confounders), large, the paper's 10 context variables merged into one environment: 100 system variables, eps = eta = 0.02, 10 context variables, mechanism changes, 100 rows per regime (1,100 rows); out of claim
cells.L10n100: L10n100: the simulation of Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen 2020 (Sec. 5.2, linear Gaussian, acyclic, with hidden confounders), larger at 100 rows per regime: 10 system variables, eps = eta = 0.25, 1 context variable, mechanism changes, 100 rows per regime (200 rows); out of claim
cells.L10n2000: L10n2000: the simulation of Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen 2020 (Sec. 5.2, linear Gaussian, acyclic, with hidden confounders), larger at 2,000 rows per regime: 10 system variables, eps = eta = 0.25, 1 context variable, mechanism changes, 2,000 rows per regime (4,000 rows); out of claim
cells.P20: P20: the simulation of Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen 2020 (Sec. 5.2, linear Gaussian, acyclic, with hidden confounders), 20 variables at the larger setting's expected degree: 20 system variables, eps = eta = 0.1184, 1 context variable, mechanism changes, 500 rows per regime (1,000 rows); out of claim
